data.title: Baking the Y Combinator from Scratch
data.author: mprast
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了Y组合子（Y Combinator），一个在函数式编程中用于实现递归的数学构造。作者强调不仅要理解“是什么”，还要理解“如何实现”和“为什么重要”。Y组合子用于在不允许显式自引用的函数式语言中实现递归。其定义为：

$$ Y = \lambda f. \enspace (\lambda x. \enspace f(x \enspace x)) \enspace (\lambda x. \enspace f(x \enspace x)) $$

文章分为两部分，第一部分解释Y组合子的构造及其如何产生固定点（fixed point），第二部分讨论其在递归中的应用。Y组合子由逻辑学家Haskell Curry提出，也被称为“固定点组合子”（Fixpoint Combinator）或“悖论组合子”（Paradoxical Combinator）。

Lambda演算中的一切都是函数，没有函数名，所有函数都是匿名函数。固定点是指对函数$f$，存在一个点$x$使得$f(x) = x$。Y组合子是一个固定点组合子，它接受一个单参数函数并返回该函数的一个固定点，满足$Y(f) = f(Y(f))$。

简言之，Y组合子通过实现固定点来支持递归，是函数式编程中一个重要工具。

主要讨论点：围绕《To Mock A Mockingbird》一书及其相关逻辑与数学概念的讨论

不同观点：
• justonceokay认为《To Mock A Mockingbird》一书前半部分深入探讨了自指谜题，后半部分则通过鸟叫声的隐喻严谨地探讨了组合逻辑，但不足之处在于全书过于依赖隐喻，未明确指出背后的数学概念。

• mkagenius提出如何记住书中内容的问题，担心即使理解了内容，也会在几周后忘记。
• mkckto提供了一个关于从Lawvere's fixed-point theorem推导Y combinator的写稿链接，为读者提供更深入的数学推导资源。
• fritzo从Löb's theorem的角度讨论了Y combinator的引用修饰版本，详细说明了如何通过添加引用符号来实现这一点。
• tromp解释了如何通过去糖化实现name = term，提供了技术细节。
• programjames从构造主义角度讨论了矛盾证明，认为矛盾证明和构造主义不矛盾，并提供了构造性证明的具体步骤。
• yayitswei以幽默方式提到最初以为会在MIT Scratch中实现这些概念，暗示了对技术实现方式的意外。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及多种资源，如书籍、视频和个人写稿，为理解自指谜题、Y combinator和组合逻辑提供了丰富的学习资料。
• 争议的焦点似乎在于《To Mock A Mockingbird》一书是否应更明确地解释数学概念，以及对矛盾证明和构造主义之间关系的不同理解。
• 技术细节上，讨论了Y combinator的不同实现方式及其在逻辑和计算机科学中的应用。

43636230.article_content:
It's a pedagogical pet peeve of mine when technical concepts are simply listed in their fully developed state, with little in the way of motivation, derivation, or historical context. This, I think, is like publishing a cookbook filled with beautiful pictures of cakes, but no recipes.
My aim with the "Baking <x> from scratch" series is to describe not only
what
, but
how
and
why
, with the hope that this will lead to a richer and more durable understanding.
The Famous Y combinator
This post is about the Y combinator. Not Y Combinator the accelerator, but the mathematical construct that it's named after -
the
Y combinator.
The Y combinator looks like this:
$$ Y = \lambda f. \enspace (\lambda x. \enspace f(x \enspace x)) \enspace (\lambda x. \enspace f(x \enspace x)) $$
Confronted with this definition, you might ask yourself:
Why does it look like that?
What is it used for?
Why do people still talk about it?
(What the heck is a combinator?)
The one-line answer to all of these is: "the Y combinator implements recursion in functional languages that don't allow for explicit self-reference", but it's worth going a little deeper than that. In my opinion, the easiest way to understand what the Y combinator
is
, at a fundamental level, is to focus on how it produces fixed points. The easiest way to understand why it's
important
is to focus on how it can be used to implement recursion. In Part 1 we'll do the former (answering 1. and half of 2. in the process) and in Part 2 we'll do the latter (answering 3. and the other half of 2.)
(We'll answer bonus question 4 later in this article!)
The Y combinator was devised by Haskell Curry, an influential logician who has the unique distinction of lending his name to both a
programming technique
and a
programming language
. It is also known as the "Fixpoint Combinator" (for reasons we'll soon discuss) and the "Paradoxical Combinator" (for reasons we'll investigate in the second half of this post.)
The Lambda Calculus
This post presumes that you're at least familiar with the lambda calculus - you don't have to be an expert, but if it's completely new to you you may have some trouble knowing what's going on.
This
is a good introduction if you need it (this article only draws on the material in Section 1.)
Two things about the lambda calculus that you should understand before reading this:
1)
everything
in the lambda calculus is a function (I'll also call these functions 'terms'.) When you "run" a program in the lambda calculus, you're basically plugging functions into other functions over and over until you can't do it anymore. This may seem like it severely limits the expressive power of the lambda calculus, but consider that we can encode different kinds of data and operators in the lambda calculus by representing them using suitable functions (the linked paper shows how to represent booleans and natural numbers in the lambda calculus, and demonstrates how to do arithmetic and some boolean algebra.) The lambda calculus is Turing Complete, so using this type of encoding you can replicate the behavior of any program written in any language.
2) There are no names besides variable names in the lambda calculus. You can't assign a name to a function and you can't call any functions by name. For the sake of readability I'll sometimes cheat and give a name to a function just to make it easier to explain. For example, I might write
$$id = \lambda x. x$$
and then later:
$$myCoolTerm = \lambda x. x \enspace id(x)$$
Just remember that you technically can't do \(name = term\) or \(name(argument)\) in the real lambda calculus; you have to write everything out. For example, \(myCoolTerm\) can only legally be written as:
$$ \lambda x. x \enspace ((\lambda x. x) (x)) $$
Y - the Fixpoint Combinator
A fixed point (or fixpoint) of a function \(f\) is a point that doesn't change when you apply \(f\) to it. In other words, \(x\) is a fixpoint of \(f\) if and only if
$$f(x) = x$$
Y is a
fixpoint
combinator
(notice I didn't say
the
fixpoint combinator - the Y combinator is one of the oldest and simplest fixpoint combinators, but there are many others!) A fixpoint combinator takes a (one-argument) function and returns some fixpoint of that function (some functions have more than one fixpoint - consider, for example, that every
value returned by an idempotent function is a fixpoint! If the function has
no
fixpoints \(Y(f)\) doesn't terminate.) So we know Y must satisfy:
$$ f(Y(f)) = Y(f)$$
but that also means:
$$Y(f) = f(Y(f))$$
From a computational perspective, this second equation says that the action of \(Y\) is to take a function and
nest itself
in a call to that function.
Because the two equations above are equivalent, finding a \(Y(f)\) that satisfies the second equation means that -
by definition
- \(Y(f)\) is a fixed point of \(f\).
Now is a good time to remember that everything in the lambda calculus is a function. So \(Y\) is a function that takes another function \(f\) and returns a fixed-p

data.title: The Columbian Orator taught nineteenth-century Americans how to speak
data.author: samclemens
data.article_summary: 《哥伦比亚演说家》是19世纪美国广受欢迎的修辞学教科书，对弗雷德里克·道格拉斯和亚伯拉罕·林肯等历史人物产生了深远影响。12岁的道格拉斯在巴尔的摩首次接触到这本书，并用辛苦赚来的50美分购买了它。这本书不仅帮助道格拉斯学会了阅读，还激发了他对演讲的热爱，最终成为他争取自由和废奴运动的重要工具。同样，年轻的林肯在伊利诺伊州新塞勒姆时也深受此书影响，通过学习其中的经典演说和启蒙思想，提升了自己的语言能力和自我认知。该书在1797年至1860年间多次再版，成为许多美国家庭的必备书籍，反映了语言在19世纪对个人成长和公众话语的重要性。

43639280.article_content:
HUMANITIES: The Magazine of the National Endowment for the Humanities
Feature
The Columbian Orator
Taught Nineteenth-Century Americans How to Speak
Among its many fans were Frederick Douglass and Abraham Lincoln
Danny Heitman
HUMANITIES, Spring 2025, Volume 46, Number 2
Photo caption
Frederick Douglass (with the title page of
The Columbian Orator
) as in the frontispiece of an 1855 edition of his autobiography.
—Wikimedia
Twitter
Facebook
One day in 1830, Frederick Douglass bought a book that changed his life. Douglass, then known as Frederick Bailey, was a twelve-year-old child enslaved in Baltimore. After hearing a group of white boys recite from
The Columbian Orator
, a grade-school textbook for teaching rhetoric, Douglass decided to get a copy for himself. Against stiff odds for slaves of the time, he learned to read, and words were his prevailing passion.
Douglass used 50 cents he’d earned working odd jobs and bought
The Columbian Orator
at a local bookshop. He fell in love with the volume and was seldom without it, carrying the book with him when he eventually escaped to freedom. With the textbook as his guide, Douglass became, in the words of biographer David W. Blight, “the greatest African American leader and orator of the nineteenth century.”
Though the legendary abolitionist read as much as he could from other sources, it’s likely that “nothing had a more immediate or lasting effect on the young Douglass’s intellectual and spiritual growth than his fortuitous discovery of
The Columbian Orator
,” Blight adds.
“Every opportunity I got, I used to read this book,” Douglass recalled. The textbook also helped shape the destiny of Douglass’s contemporary Abraham Lincoln during Lincoln’s early days in New Salem, Illinois. With little formal education, the twenty-one-year-old Lincoln “studied with relish the classical and Enlightenment-era oratory in
The Columbian Orator
during his first winter (1831–32) in New Salem on the Illinois prairie,” Blight tells readers.
In
Giants
, his 2008 book about striking parallels between Douglass and Lincoln, historian John Stauffer notes the big impact that
The Columbian Orator
had on both of their lives. Like Douglass, young Lincoln “was hungry for knowledge, and it was one of the few books he read during his formative years, along with a spelling book, the Bible, and one or two others,” Stauffer observes in recounting the role of the classic textbook in forming the future president.
For strivers like Lincoln, guides to rhetoric had a special currency in the nineteenth century. “Lincoln was born into a national culture in which language was the most widely available key to individual growth and achievement. It dominated public discourse,” scholar Fred Kaplan tells readers of his book,
Lincoln: The Biography of a Writer
. “No TVs, DVDs, computers, movie screens, radios, or electricity, and no sound bites. Language mattered because it was useful for practical communication and for learning and because it could shape and direct people’s feelings and thoughts in a culture in which spoken or written words had no rival. In Lincoln’s case it also mattered immensely because it was the tool by which he explored and defined himself.”
Douglass and Lincoln were far from alone in embracing
The Columbian Orator
, which was first published by New England educator Caleb Bingham in 1797. “The
Orator
was one of the most popular books in the new nation,” Stauffer points out. “From 1797 to 1860, it went through some 23 editions and in many American homes it was one of a handful of essential books, along with the Bible, a spelling book, and a farmer’s almanac.”
To get some idea of
The Columbian Orator’
s important role in early America, it’s perhaps best to start with its title. Although the textbook’s name might sound strange to modern ears, it would have resonated with people in Douglass and Lincoln’s time. In 1790, Congress had created the District of Columbia as the new seat of government, a nod to explorer Christopher Columbus. Even earlier, Americans had evoked a mythical heroine, Columbia, as a symbol of the emerging nation. “She was portrayed as a goddess, draped in a neoclassical gown and holding a sword, an olive branch and a laurel wreath as metaphors for justice, peace and victory,” journalist Cari Shane noted in a 2023 history of Columbia. “As Lady Columbia’s image spread across the country, particularly after the Revolution, she came to embody the nation’s highest aspirations—and its colonial ambitions. Though largely forgotten today, she reigned for two centuries as our collective emblem, and her biography offers a tale in miniature of the development of a young democracy.”
Before she was eclipsed by the Statue of Liberty as a national symbol, Columbia personified the ideals of a young republic trying to reconcile the virtues of classical antiquity with the dynamism of a country on the move.

data.title: Parser Combinators Beat Regexes
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在Haskell中使用正则表达式和解析器组合子解决Advent of Code问题的对比。作者首先展示了一个使用正则表达式库`pcre-heavy`处理字节字符串的解决方案，该方案能解决问题但性能较差，且存在隐含的假设（如捕获组的数量），可能导致未来运行时错误。接着，作者提供了一个基于attoparsec解析器库的解决方案，尽管代码更复杂，但更加可靠和易于维护。Haskell社区通常偏好解析器组合子而非正则表达式，因为它们更灵活且类型安全。正则表达式适用于简单情况，但在复杂或需要高性能的场景中，解析器组合子更具优势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：正则表达式（regex）与解析器（parser）的选择与使用

不同观点：
• Rendello认为使用正则表达式进行词法分析可以简化很多工作，尤其在不需要解析编程语言时，正则表达式足够应付需求。
• yen223支持解析器组合子（parser combinators）的强大功能，认为它通过将复杂问题分解为简单的读取标记问题，使得解析变得更易理解，但遗憾的是它不太可能成为主流。
• austin-cheney指出正则表达式适用于简单的搜索任务，而全功能的解析器则更适合需要智能处理的场景，尽管其成本更高。
• kazinator讨论了Haskell中正则表达式的实现细节，指出其依赖的PCRE库并不是真正的正则表达式，而是具有回溯功能的扩展版本。
• arn3n认为在Haskell中编写解析器虽然常见，但自己更倾向于使用正则表达式，因为解析器的代码往往过于复杂。
• pklausler分享了使用解析器组合子处理复杂问题的经验，特别是在处理Fortran解析时的优势，但也提到性能问题需要注意。
• o11c提醒大多数解析器组合子和正则表达式的实现可能在处理时间上呈指数级增长，不适合处理不可信输入。
• maxbond认为解析器组合子在语法描述和手写解析器之间提供了一个很好的折中方案，甚至可以结合正则表达式使用。
• kreig从理论上指出，解析器组合子能够解析的语法范围比正则表达式更广，依据是Chomsky层级。
• DadBase幽默地指出，在处理如CSV等实际问题时，简单的工具如awk和一些技巧可能更可靠。
• torginus认为函数式语言特别适合编写解析器，但解析器组合子在效率和功能上不如定制解决方案，且主要用于功能性语言的文化中。
• asQuirreL认为正则表达式和解析器各有其适用场景，不应简单对立，建议将结构识别和求值分开处理。
• virgilp从自动机理论角度分析，指出解析器组合子生成的下推自动机比正则表达式生成的确定性有限自动机更强大，但在正则表达式领域内，后者更高效。
• smcl推荐了C#中的Sprache库作为创建小解析器的一个实用工具，认为正则表达式在某些任务中显得笨重。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点主要在于解析器组合子和正则表达式在不同场景下的适用性和效率。
• 讨论中提到了Haskell、Erlang和JavaScript等不同语言中解析器和正则表达式的实现和应用经验。
• 性能和复杂性是选择解析器或正则表达式的重要考虑因素，特别是在处理实际问题和不可信输入时。

43638422.article_content:
Someone online was solving Advent of Code problems, and had a question about
last years’ day 3
. They had a working solution using regular expressions
(regexes) on
String
values, but they wanted to use
ByteString
values instead
for performance reasons. They were surprised, however, that there seems to be a
lack of community cohesion around regex libraries in Haskell.
There’s a reason for that. We generally don’t use regexes in Haskell. We use
parser combinators instead, because they are almost always better. In other
languages, it would be considered overkill to write a full parser when a simple
regex can do the same thing. In Haskell, writing a parser is no big deal. We
just do it and move on with our lives.
The regex solution
The first part of the Advent of Code problem is well suited for a regex-based
solution. Here’s what such a solution might look like in Haskell. It uses the
pcre-heavy
Haskell library which in turn calls out to the system-wide
pcre
C library for actually compiling and running the regex.
In[1]:
{-# LANGUAGE QuasiQuotes #-}
module
Main
where
import
Data.ByteString
(
ByteString
)
import
qualified
Data.ByteString.Char8
as
Char8
import
Data.Monoid
(
Sum
(
..
))
import
qualified
Text.Regex.PCRE.Heavy
as
Re
import
Text.Regex.PCRE.Heavy
(re)
test_input
::
ByteString
test_input
=
Char8.pack
"xmul(2,4)%&mul[3,7]!@^do_not_mul(5,5)+mul(32,64]then(mul(11,8)mul(8,5))"
regex_matches
::
ByteString
->
Int
regex_matches
input
=
let
--
Get a list of regex matches with numbers extracted.
--
The 're' quasi-quoter compiles the regex at compile
--
time, avoiding the runtime cost of that.
hits
=
Re.scan [re
|mul\((\d+),(\d+)\)|
] input
--
Take one hit and compute its product, converting the
--
stringified numbers into actual numbers, then wrapping
--
it up as a term in a sum.
compute (
_
, [a, b])
=
Sum
(read (Char8.unpack a)
*
read (Char8.unpack b))
in
--
Fold up all terms in the sum into a single number.
getSum (foldMap compute hits)
main
::
IO
()
main
=
do
print (regex_matches test_input)
This does the job and returns the expected sum of 161. If we run this on just
under a megabyte of input data, it takes 19 seconds on my machine, spending
almost all of that time inside the
pcre
library.
1
1
Though this is a little
strange, because if I do the same thing in Perl, it takes 0.02 seconds. I wish I
had time to investigate what goes wrong.
But the main thing I dislike about this is that there’s a very strong implicit
contract between the regex and the
compute
function. The
compute
function
assumes that there were exactly two capturing groups and that they are strings
that can safely be converted to integers. This is true, but there’s nothing in
the code making that guarantee. If those assumptions become violated a year from
now, that would not be a compiler error but an exception that interrupts the
production service at 3
am
the day before an important customer meeting.
The parser solution
For the sort of problem we are facing here, the parser-based solution does look
more complicated at first glance. Part of the reason is that the regex library
comes with a method that gets all matches, regardless of their position in the
input. Parser combinators are meant to be written to consume all of the input,
so we have to manually write the parser code that iterates the input and finds
the next match.
This solution uses the
attoparsec
library, which is made to work with
ByteString
values specifically, since the person who asked the question seemed
to care about performance.
In[2]:
module
Main
where
import
Control.Applicative
((
<|>
))
import
qualified
Data.Attoparsec.ByteString.Char8
as
Parser
import
Data.ByteString
(
ByteString
)
import
qualified
Data.ByteString.Char8
as
Char8
import
qualified
Data.Either
as
Either
test_input
::
ByteString
test_input
=
Char8.pack
"xmul(2,4)%&mul[3,7]!@^do_not_mul(5,5)+mul(32,64]then(mul(11,8)mul(8,5))"
parser_matches
::
ByteString
->
Int
parser_matches
input
=
let
--
Parse a mul instruction. Starts by reading the opening
--
sequence, then the first value, then the separator,
--
then the second value, then the terminator. Finally,
--
it returns the product of the pair of values.
mul
=
do
Parser.string (Char8.pack
"mul("
)
first
<-
Parser.decimal
Parser.char
','
second
<-
Parser.decimal
Parser.char
')'
pure (first
*
second)
--
Parse the next mul instruction. Start by trying to
--
parse a mul instruction immediately. If that fails,
--
instead (1) advance the parser one step, and
--
(2) try again.
next
=
mul
<|>
do
Parser.anyChar
next
--
Scan the entire input for all mul instructions,
--
returning the sum of their products.
scan
=
do
muls
<-
Parser.many1 next
pure (sum muls)
in
--
Run the parser over the input,
--
handling a parse error by throwing
--
an exception.
Either.fromRight (error
"Failed to parse input."
)
(Parser.parseOnly scan input)
main
::
IO
()
main
=
do
print (parser_matches test_input)
This is written in what one might call
direct, monadic
style, doing just what
was requ

data.title: Men's Weird Collections Inspired the Modern Museum: Cabinets of Curiosities
data.author: crescit_eundo
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：博物馆和奇异收藏品的趋势及个人体验

不同观点：
• [eszed] 认为一些博物馆正在远离“奇异收藏”的风格，变得更加“体面”和现代化。他举了伦敦的Horniman博物馆和埃克塞特的RAMM博物馆作为例子，并推荐了牛津的Pitt-Rivers博物馆，认为它是一个独特的奇异收藏体验，但如果重新策展可能会失去这种魅力。
• [hodgesrm] 提到了与飞行器相关的奇异收藏，推荐了加州的Hiller Aviation Museum，特别是其中的可折叠直升机，这是一种为战斗中被击落的飞行员设计的逃生工具。
• [kurthr] 推荐了洛杉矶的Museum of Jurassic Technology，认为它具有一些令人难以置信的展品，是一个值得参观的地方。
• [rambambram] 分享了自己在家中设立的“奇异柜”收藏，包括从各地收集来的石头、陨石（或恐龙粪便）、佛像和埃菲尔铁塔模型，并期待添加更多奇异物品。
• [moomin] 推荐了伦敦的John Soane's博物馆和Hunterian博物馆，指出后者展示了现代医疗器具的发展，并与Soane's博物馆的传统体验形成对比。
• [ChrisMarshallNY] 提到了一集Connections节目，与讨论的文章相关，但未深入展开。
• [spacechild1] 介绍了维也纳的病理学博物馆（Narrenturm），其中有历史上的奇异收藏品，提醒该博物馆可能不适合胆小者参观。

补充讨论：
• [metalman] 探讨了收集奇异物品的心理和社会因素，认为这是一种本能或社会行为，并分享了朋友通过买卖奇异物品为生的经历，称之为“捕捉与释放”。他还提到了一些人对物品产生的特殊癖好和痴迷。

争议焦点：
• 博物馆是否应保持传统的奇异收藏风格还是转向更加现代化的策展方式，以提高其“体面性”和教育价值。这涉及到对博物馆功能的认识和个人对奇异收藏体验的偏好。

data.title: Learning to Program with Haiku
data.author: nivethan
data.article_summary: 《Learning to Program with Haiku》是由DarkWyrm编写的一系列编程教学，旨在帮助没有编程基础的人学习为Haiku操作系统编写简单程序。这些课程于2010年1月开始发布，采用Creative Commons许可协议，允许非商业用途的免费分发。课程从基础编程概念开始，逐步讲解数据类型、条件判断、循环、数组、指针、内存管理等，最终引导学习者使用C++和Haiku API编写图形用户界面（GUI）程序。每节课都包含PDF下载和评论查看功能，课程结构包括多个单元和复习，帮助学习者循序渐进掌握编程技能。第14课之后，学习者将能够编写简单的GUI程序。课程资源和支持可通过Lulu.com获取。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Haiku和BeOS操作系统的技术特点、历史发展及其对编程教育的影响的不同看法。

不同观点：
• [interroboink, DeathArrow] 提到了Neal Stephenson对BeOS的评价，并通过一篇旧的BeOS错误报告幽默地表达了对该系统的怀念。DeathArrow进一步探讨了BeOS未能广泛普及的遗憾，以及对现代操作系统缺乏创新的失望。

• [tialaramex] 分析了Haiku项目的技术细节，指出其代码库包含大量旧的C++ 98甚至更早的代码，以及从BeOS继承的非标准代码块，如BString和BList。他还提到Haiku中存在许多临时采用的BSD代码，这些代码原本计划替换但未实现。

• [Hj8Rd2Qw] 赞扬了Haiku在编程教学方面的创新方法，认为其从一开始就让学习者接触实际的GUI应用程序，有助于更直观地理解编程概念，并能产生可见的成果。

• [codr7] 分享了自己对BeOS的使用体验，指出BeOS的API由于其多线程特性而具有挑战性，但整体上仍然是一个非常优秀的操作系统。

• [ktallett] 描述了自己在C++编程和应用移植方面的积极经验，并认为Haiku如今已经发展到可以作为日常使用的操作系统。

• [Aldipower] 对Haiku教程的易读性和易理解性表示赞赏，认为它是学习C编程的好资源。

• [revskill] 提出疑问，认为对于已经会编程的人来说，Haiku的必要性不大。

补充讨论：
• [DeathArrow] 表达了对过去多种操作系统百花齐放时代的怀念，并质疑为何现代操作系统领域被Windows和类Unix系统垄断，期待有新的操作系统概念和实现出现。

• [dddw] 简单表达了对Haiku的喜爱和支持。

争议焦点：
• Haiku和BeOS在现代操作系统环境中的地位和必要性。DeathArrow对现有操作系统的局限性感到不满，而revskill则质疑Haiku对于有经验程序员的价值。

In January of 2010, I started publishing lessons on learning to program for
Haiku, aimed at people who want to be able to write simple
programs to get stuff done, but never had anyone around teach them. Years ago,
I started teaching myself and am an active developer. It's my turn to give back.
All of these lessons are distributed under a Creative Commons license which
allows free distribution for noncommercial purposes. Should you have questions,
by all means
contact me

43640403.article_summary: 《Learning to Program with Haiku》是由DarkWyrm编写的一系列编程教学，旨在帮助没有编程基础的人学习为Haiku操作系统编写简单程序。这些课程于2010年1月开始发布，采用Creative Commons许可协议，允许非商业用途的免费分发。课程从基础编程概念开始，逐步讲解数据类型、条件判断、循环、数组、指针、内存管理等，最终引导学习者使用C++和Haiku API编写图形用户界面（GUI）程序。每节课都包含PDF下载和评论查看功能，课程结构包括多个单元和复习，帮助学习者循序渐进掌握编程技能。第14课之后，学习者将能够编写简单的GUI程序。课程资源和支持可通过Lulu.com获取。
43640403.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Haiku和BeOS操作系统的技术特点、历史发展及其对编程教育的影响的不同看法。

不同观点：
• [interroboink, DeathArrow] 提到了Neal Stephenson对BeOS的评价，并通过一篇旧的BeOS错误报告幽默地表达了对该系统的怀念。DeathArrow进一步探讨了BeOS未能广泛普及的遗憾，以及对现代操作系统缺乏创新的失望。

• [tialaramex] 分析了Haiku项目的技术细节，指出其代码库包含大量旧的C++ 98甚至更早的代码，以及从BeOS继承的非标准代码块，如BString和BList。他还提到Haiku中存在许多临时采用的BSD代码，这些代码原本计划替换但未实现。

• [Hj8Rd2Qw] 赞扬了Haiku在编程教学方面的创新方法，认为其从一开始就让学习者接触实际的GUI应用程序，有助于更直观地理解编程概念，并能产生可见的成果。

• [codr7] 分享了自己对BeOS的使用体验，指出BeOS的API由于其多线程特性而具有挑战性，但整体上仍然是一个非常优秀的操作系统。

• [ktallett] 描述了自己在C++编程和应用移植方面的积极经验，并认为Haiku如今已经发展到可以作为日常使用的操作系统。

• [Aldipower] 对Haiku教程的易读性和易理解性表示赞赏，认为它是学习C编程的好资源。

• [revskill] 提出疑问，认为对于已经会编程的人来说，Haiku的必要性不大。

补充讨论：
• [DeathArrow] 表达了对过去多种操作系统百花齐放时代的怀念，并质疑为何现代操作系统领域被Windows和类Unix系统垄断，期待有新的操作系统概念和实现出现。

• [dddw] 简单表达了对Haiku的喜爱和支持。

争议焦点：
• Haiku和BeOS在现代操作系统环境中的地位和必要性。DeathArrow对现有操作系统的局限性感到不满，而revskill则质疑Haiku对于有经验程序员的价值。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Emacs窗口管理功能及其使用体验

不同观点：
• [globnomulous] 赞赏一名高中生程序员开发了Emacs的窗口管理功能，并分享了相关链接。
• [masutaka] 提到自己创建了一个用于切换窗口垂直和水平分割的自定义功能，并分享了代码链接。
• [gumbojuice] 表示自己很少使用Emacs的窗口功能，更注重屏幕空间专注于单一任务，质疑是否错过了某些实用功能。
• [kfajdsl] 分享了自己的使用场景，指出在关闭大垂直窗格后需要重新创建布局的痛点，认为新功能会很有帮助。
• [eddieh] 对讨论中Emacs的"frames"和"windows”术语感到困惑，指出这些术语与常规用法相反。
• [taeric] 询问如何在桌面窗口管理中实现类似功能，表示有意在PopOS上设置键盘宏，但不知从何入手，并考虑制作Gnome插件。
• [a_e_k] 提到自己已经有一个类似的自定义功能，很高兴Emacs核心现在有了等效功能，可以简化自己的配置。
• [taeric]（再次）认为这些功能比预想中更有用，正在寻找方法将它们变成习惯动作，并询问其他人是否有推荐的键绑定。
• [smurpy] 使用43英寸4K电视作为主显示器，全屏Emacs窗口分割成多个窗格，难以理解其他人如何在没有类似配置的情况下高效工作。
• [mediumsmart] 使用macOS，习惯于将浏览器和Emacs窗口分屏，最大化利用垂直分割，并在需要时打开全屏框架，其他缓冲区则在后台待命。
• [malicka] 表示自己一直在使用一种拙劣的水平镜像方法，很高兴发现有更好的解决方案，并对作者表示感谢。
• [smitty1e] 强调Emacs无论是否有桌面环境或在终端中工作都能很好地运行，认为这虽然听起来有点奇怪但很有用。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及Emacs的"frames"和"windows"术语的混淆，部分用户对此感到困惑。
• 用户分享了各自使用Emacs窗口管理功能的具体场景和配置，包括多窗格、全屏和键盘宏等。
• 部分用户对如何将Emacs的窗口管理功能应用到桌面环境（如PopOS和Gnome）表示兴趣，并寻求建议。
• 用户对新功能的实用性和使用体验持积极态度，并分享了各自的键绑定和配置建议。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Chromebook硬件的支持情况及其对开源社区和用户的影响

不同观点：
• candreasen：认为Chromebook受益于之前对rk3399芯片的上游支持工作，特别是pine64 pinebook pro也使用了该芯片。这种上游工作不仅使pine客户受益，还惠及整个社区。
• bradley_taunt：提供了存档链接，但未明确表达立场，可能旨在提供更多信息供参考。
• extraduder_ire：赞赏Google要求Chromebook的引导加载程序可解锁的决定，认为这使得许多设备在支持结束后仍能保持有用，避免成为电子废物。
• TheCycoONE：提到Libreboot支持这些设备，可以移除ChromeOS的限制，并分享了安装指南和外部刷写的经验。还称赞了Alyssa开发的panfrost GPU驱动程序对Linux体验的显著改善。
• kcb：推荐Thinkpad x13s作为支持良好的ARM架构Linux笔记本，认为其性价比高且性能足以满足日常使用。
• Mashimo：指出服务器当前宕机的问题，未就设备支持发表明确观点。
• interglossa：分享了个人使用经历，表示在2019年购买的Chromebook仍在日常使用，尽管更新早已停止。
• megous：认为这些设备有上游内核/u-boot支持，使用最新内核应该能顺利运行。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：虽然没有直接的争议，但隐含的对比在于是否所有Chromebook都能像rk3399支持的那样顺利获得开源社区的支持。
• 重要论据：
  - 上游支持工作对社区的广泛益处。
  - 可解锁的引导加载程序对设备长期使用的重要性。
  - Libreboot和外部刷写的实际应用经验。
  - 特定驱动程序（如panfrost GPU驱动）对Linux体验的显著提升。
  - 推荐其他替代设备（如Thinkpad x13s）作为Linux笔记本的选择。

这些观点共同构成了关于Chromebook硬件支持及其对用户和社区影响的广泛讨论。

data.title: Smartfunc: Turn Docstrings into LLM-Functions
data.author: alexmolas
data.article_summary:
`smartfunc` 是一个将 docstrings 转换为 LLM（大语言模型）功能的 Python 库，基于 Simon Willison 的 `llm` 库构建。通过使用装饰器，开发者可以轻松地将函数的文档字符串转换为 LLM 提示，并使用指定的后端（如 GPT-4）生成结果。该库支持使用 Jinja2 模板和 Pydantic 模型定义响应结构，允许通过 `.env` 文件存储 API 密钥，并具有异步支持和多供应商生态系统。其目标是在快速原型设计中提供简洁的解决方案，专注于简单易用，而非复杂的功能集。以下是一个示例：

```python
from smartfunc import backend
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Summary(BaseModel):
    summary: str
    pros: list[str]
    cons: list[str]

@backend("gpt-4o-mini", system="You are a helpful assistant.", temperature=0.5)
def generate_poke_desc(text: str) -> Summary:
    """Describe the following pokemon: {{ text }}"""
    pass

print(generate_poke_desc("pikachu"))
```

这个库的主要优势在于其简洁性和对特定功能集的专注，适用于快速原型设计和简单任务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在编码中的应用及其实现方式

不同观点：
• **将LLM视为编译器**：[lukev]认为，将LLM视为编译器比视为初级开发者更具可扩展性、可组合性和可扩展性。这种方法更符合未来的发展趋势。

• **LLM在编码中的进展及应用**：[shaism]提到，过去在个人项目中实现过类似功能，但如今的LLM在编码方面更加熟练，甚至可以通过装饰器方法根据Docstring自动生成Python代码，促进编写明确的文档并保证一致性。

• **对不同编程语言的需求**：[_1tan]询问是否有适用于Java的类似工具，显示出对LLM在不同编程语言中应用的关注。

• **函数与不同LLM的兼容性问题**：[senko]指出，许多采用相同方法的库存在缺陷，无法在运行时轻松使用不同的LLM，建议通过显式传递LLM对象来提高灵活性，并提供了具体示例。

• **与其他工具的集成**：[simonw]对LLM与 schema 功能的集成表示赞赏，并提供了相关链接以供参考。

• **模型优化方向**：[asadm]设想将功能函数提炼成微型模型，而不是通过API调用基础模型，以提高效率和性能。

• **类似工具的比较**：[noddybear]提到一个类似工具Tanuki，并提供了链接。

• **对Docstring的看法**：[nonethewiser]认为，虽然自动生成Docstring的功能很有用，但手写Docstring很繁琐，且LLM对普通文本描述处理得也不错，因此质疑Docstring是否真的优于纯文本描述。

• **其他工具推荐**：[miki123211]提到promptic，并认为litellm是一个更好的Python库，因为它支持更多模型提供者且不需要插件。

补充讨论：
• **LLM在代码注释中的应用**：[dheera]分享了反向使用LLM的经验，即在难以理解的代码中插入注释，通过提示LLM“大量注释这段代码”来提高可读性。

争议焦点：
• **LLM在编码中作为编译器还是开发者的角色更优**：[lukev]与潜在反对者可能在LLM角色的最佳定位上存在分歧，一方认为编译器模型更优，另一方可能认为开发者模型更具灵活性。

• **Docstring的价值**：部分用户如[shaism]强调了明确Docstring的重要性，而[nonethewiser]则认为纯文本描述可能更简便且足够。

How does it work?
This library wraps around the
llm library
made by
Simon Willison
. The docstring is parsed and turned into a Jinja2 template which we inject with variables to generate a prompt at runtime. We then use the backend given by the decorator to run the prompt and return the result.
The

43619884.article_summary:
`smartfunc` 是一个将 docstrings 转换为 LLM（大语言模型）功能的 Python 库，基于 Simon Willison 的 `llm` 库构建。通过使用装饰器，开发者可以轻松地将函数的文档字符串转换为 LLM 提示，并使用指定的后端（如 GPT-4）生成结果。该库支持使用 Jinja2 模板和 Pydantic 模型定义响应结构，允许通过 `.env` 文件存储 API 密钥，并具有异步支持和多供应商生态系统。其目标是在快速原型设计中提供简洁的解决方案，专注于简单易用，而非复杂的功能集。以下是一个示例：

```python
from smartfunc import backend
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Summary(BaseModel):
    summary: str
    pros: list[str]
    cons: list[str]

@backend("gpt-4o-mini", system="You are a helpful assistant.", temperature=0.5)
def generate_poke_desc(text: str) -> Summary:
    """Describe the following pokemon: {{ text }}"""
    pass

print(generate_poke_desc("pikachu"))
```

这个库的主要优势在于其简洁性和对特定功能集的专注，适用于快速原型设计和简单任务。

主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在编码中的应用及其实现方式

不同观点：
• **将LLM视为编译器**：[lukev]认为，将LLM视为编译器比视为初级开发者更具可扩展性、可组合性和可扩展性。这种方法更符合未来的发展趋势。

• **LLM在编码中的进展及应用**：[shaism]提到，过去在个人项目中实现过类似功能，但如今的LLM在编码方面更加熟练，甚至可以通过装饰器方法根据Docstring自动生成Python代码，促进编写明确的文档并保证一致性。

• **对不同编程语言的需求**：[_1tan]询问是否有适用于Java的类似工具，显示出对LLM在不同编程语言中应用的关注。

• **函数与不同LLM的兼容性问题**：[senko]指出，许多采用相同方法的库存在缺陷，无法在运行时轻松使用不同的LLM，建议通过显式传递LLM对象来提高灵活性，并提供了具体示例。

• **与其他工具的集成**：[simonw]对LLM与 schema 功能的集成表示赞赏，并提供了相关链接以供参考。

• **模型优化方向**：[asadm]设想将功能函数提炼成微型模型，而不是通过API调用基础模型，以提高效率和性能。

• **类似工具的比较**：[noddybear]提到一个类似工具Tanuki，并提供了链接。

• **对Docstring的看法**：[nonethewiser]认为，虽然自动生成Docstring的功能很有用，但手写Docstring很繁琐，且LLM对普通文本描述处理得也不错，因此质疑Docstring是否真的优于纯文本描述。

• **其他工具推荐**：[miki123211]提到promptic，并认为litellm是一个更好的Python库，因为它支持更多模型提供者且不需要插件。

补充讨论：
• **LLM在代码注释中的应用**：[dheera]分享了反向使用LLM的经验，即在难以理解的代码中插入注释，通过提示LLM“大量注释这段代码”来提高可读性。

争议焦点：
• **LLM在编码中作为编译器还是开发者的角色更优**：[lukev]与潜在反对者可能在LLM角色的最佳定位上存在分歧，一方认为编译器模型更优，另一方可能认为开发者模型更具灵活性。

• **Docstring的价值**：部分用户如[shaism]强调了明确Docstring的重要性，而[nonethewiser]则认为纯文本描述可能更简便且足够。

data.author: sebg
data.article_summary: 本文以幽默和隐喻的方式探讨了Python编程中的简洁与优雅。作者强调Python的“Zen”，即追求唯一且明显的方式解决问题，并通过古怪的代码示例展示了如何用特殊语法表示数字1和更大的整数。文章还提到计算机程序本质上是位流，鼓励读者理解基本原理。最终，作者展示了一个复杂的Python示例，用以说明掌握基础后可以编写的典型程序。全文以趣味方式传达了Python编程的美学和哲学。

主要讨论点：Python及JavaScript中的特殊语法和代码行为

不同观点：
• **plus** 解释了Python中的Ellipsis对象及其在布尔和算术运算中的表现。他详细说明了`--(...==...)`如何通过布尔和负号操作得出结果为2，并提到这种写法是具有调侃性质的，并非严肃推荐。
• **maxloh** 展示了在JavaScript中类似的复杂写法，通过使用类似JSFuck的技巧实现简单功能（如`alert(1)`），表明这种复杂写法不仅限于Python。
• **mariocesar** 提到，使用Ellipsis的结果可以执行打印语句`print('hello, world')`，暗示这些特殊语法在实际中可能有意外的副作用。
• **MadVikingGod** 提供了一个自定义类来模拟Ellipsis的行为，展示了如何通过定义`__neg__`和`__sub__`方法实现类似的算术操作。他认为这种技巧对所有人来说都是有趣的Python用法。
• **benob** 提到他学到了Python中`1--2==3`的特殊语法行为，表明这种写法可能让人感到意外。
• **elijahbenizzy** 对JavaScript中的类似技巧表示兴趣，希望看到JavaScript中的实现。
• **callamdelaney** 表达了对Python语法逐渐变得复杂的担忧，认为这种趋势并不理想。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Python语法是否变得过于复杂。一些用户（如callamdelaney）对这种趋势表示不满，认为增加了理解和维护代码的难度。
• 另一个值得注意的点是，这些特殊语法和行为虽然有趣，但在实际开发中可能并不常用，且容易导致代码可读性下降。
• 讨论中也涉及了不同语言（Python和JavaScript）中类似技巧的实现，展示了跨语言的共性。

data.title: Isaac Asimov describes how AI will liberate humans and their creativity (1992)
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: In his last major interview in 1992, Isaac Asimov discussed artificial intelligence (AI) as technology that takes over mundane tasks previously done by humans, such as alphabetizing or arithmetic. He envisioned a future where AI liberates humans from routine work, allowing them to focus on more creative endeavors. Asimov believed AI and human intelligence are complementary, with each enhancing the other's capabilities. He acknowledged potential challenges with technological advancements but emphasized the importance of preparing for them. Asimov also compared the rise of AI to the invention of the automobile, cautioning against reshaping society entirely around new technology and suggesting the preservation of human-scale elements from the pre-AI world.

Isaac Asimov Describes How Artificial Intelligence Will Liberate Humans & Their Creativity: Watch His Last Major Interview (1992)
in
Artificial Intelligence
,
Technology
|   	April 8th, 2025
Leave a Comment
Arti­fi­cial intel­li­gence may be one of the major top­ics of our his­tor­i­cal moment, but it can be sur­pris­ing­ly tricky to define. In
the more than 30-year-old inter­view clip above
, Isaac Asi­mov describes arti­fi­cial intel­li­gence as “a phrase that we use for any device that does things which, in the past, we have asso­ci­at­ed only with human intel­li­gence.” At one time, not so very long before, “only human beings could alpha­bet­ize cards”; in the machines that could even then do it in a frac­tion of a sec­ond, “you’ve got an exam­ple of arti­fi­cial intel­li­gence.” Not that humans were ever espe­cial­ly good at card alpha­bet­i­za­tion, nor at arith­metic: “the cheap­est com­put­er in the world can mul­ti­ply and divide more accu­rate­ly than we can.”
You could see arti­fi­cial intel­li­gence as a kind of fron­tier, then, which moves for­ward as com­put­er­ized machines take over the tasks humans pre­vi­ous­ly had to do them­selves. “Every indus­try, the gov­ern­ment itself, tax-col­lect­ing agen­cies, air­planes: every­thing depends on com­put­ers. We have per­son­al com­put­ers in the home, and they are con­stant­ly get­ting bet­ter, cheap­er, more ver­sa­tile, capa­ble of doing more things, so that we can look into the future, when, for the first time, human­i­ty in gen­er­al will be freed from all kinds of work that’s real­ly an insult to the human brain.” Such work “requires no great thought, no great cre­ativ­i­ty. Leave all that to the com­put­er, and we can leave to our­selves those things that com­put­ers can’t do.”
This inter­view was shot for
Isaac Asi­mov’s Visions of the Future
, a tele­vi­sion doc­u­men­tary that aired in 1992, the last year of its sub­jec­t’s life. One won­ders what Asi­mov would make of the world of 2025, and whether he’d still see arti­fi­cial and nat­ur­al intel­li­gence as com­ple­men­tary, rather than in com­pe­ti­tion. “They work togeth­er,” he argues. “Each sup­plies the lack of the oth­er. And in coop­er­a­tion, they can advance far more rapid­ly than either could by itself.” But as a sci­ence-fic­tion nov­el­ist, he could hard­ly fail to acknowl­edge that tech­no­log­i­cal progress does­n’t come easy: “Will there be dif­fi­cul­ties? Undoubt­ed­ly. Will there be things that we won’t like? Undoubt­ed­ly. But we’ve got to think about it now, so as to be pre­pared for pos­si­ble unpleas­ant­ness and try to guard against it before it’s too late.”
These are fair points, though it’s what comes next that most stands out to the twen­ty-first-cen­tu­ry mind. “It’s like in the old days, when the auto­mo­bile was invent­ed,” Asi­mov says. “It would’ve been so much bet­ter if we had built our cities with the auto­mo­bile in mind, instead of build­ing cities for a pre-auto­mo­bile age and find­ing we can hard­ly find any place to put the auto­mo­biles or allow them to dri­ve.” Yet the cities we most enjoy today aren’t the new metrop­o­lis­es built or great­ly expand­ed in the car-ori­ent­ed decades after the Sec­ond World War, but pre­cise­ly those old ones whose streets were built to the seem­ing­ly obso­lete scale of human beings on foot. Per­haps, upon reflec­tion, we’d do best by future gen­er­a­tions to keep as many ele­ments of the pre-AI world around as we pos­si­bly can.

Asimov also compared the rise of AI to the invention of the automobile, cautioning against reshaping society entirely around new technology and suggesting the preservation of human-scale elements from the pre-AI world.

data.author: sohkamyung
data.article_summary: 神经生物学家Dragana Rogulja的团队研究了睡眠剥夺对果蝇和小鼠的影响，发现缺乏睡眠的动物大约十天后会开始死亡，当它们每晚失去约90%的睡眠时。这一发现表明睡眠对维持生命至关重要，且其影响不仅限于大脑。研究揭示，睡眠不足会导致果蝇肠道中的活性氧（ROS）浓度升高，从而引发死亡。这表明睡眠在维持全身稳态中起关键作用，而不仅是大脑的休息。ROS的积累主要发生在肠道，而非大脑，这提示睡眠对全身健康的调节至关重要。借助现代技术如光遗传学和聚焦超声，研究人员正逐渐揭示睡眠如何通过基因、代谢和激素的调节来保持生物体稳态，从而避免细胞功能失效。

Credit: Alexandra Vaccaro and Yosef Kaplan Dor
When neurobiologist Dragana Rogulja began studying sleep in her laboratory at Harvard Medical School in Boston, Massachusetts, in 2013, she had no idea what her experiments would tell her about how sleep affects the body. She wasn’t assuming — as many people do — that it’s a function mainly of the brain. She was just starting her lab and decided to throw the net wide, asking the question: if animals are sleep deprived, how long will it take until they die — and when they die, what is the specific cause?
She expected it would take years to answer these questions. But in six months, Rogulja’s postdoctoral assistant, Alexandra Vaccaro, found a tantalizing clue.
“We started looking at lifespan and saw that the moment when sleep-deprived animals would start dying was pretty much always the same,” Rogulja says. “When they lost about 90% of their sleep each night, they started dying within about ten days.” Those studies were in flies and mice — but the implications for other animals, including humans, was intriguing.
The average adult spends more than 20 years of their life sleeping, and the consequences of not getting enough are clearly harmful. But surprisingly little is known about why it’s necessary. That is, in part, because only in the past couple of decades have the tools become available to help scientists to understand the fundamental biological function of sleep. These include optogenetics, which involves directing laser light to specific neurons to wake a person or put them into deep sleep, and focused ultrasound, which has emerged in the past five years as a way to view the deep-brain neural oscillations that occur during sleep.
With the help of such tools, researchers are beginning to understand that sleep does more than just give our brains and bodies a respite from the rigours of the day. When we sleep, our genes, metabolism and hormones are regulated through increasing or slowing of their activity.
Finding homeostasis
What’s the most important function of the brain? It might be tempting to say a specific task, such as communicating, finding food or avoiding predators. But none of these roles is possible if the brain’s cellular machinery isn’t functioning reliably. Indeed, it is maintaining that reliability that might well be the main purpose of sleep, says Keith Hengen, a neuroscientist at Washington University in St. Louis, Missouri.
Nature Outlook: Sleep
“This was like a light bulb for me a long time ago,” Hengen says. In terms of machine learning, “if you have a deep-learning network, and you continue to let it learn, it’ll exhibit catastrophic forgetting — the wheels come off and the thing stops. It just fails.”
Biology has solved this problem of brain overload by resetting to a ‘critical point’ — a process that occurs mainly during sleep. During the day, the brain is consumed with the many things it has to do, such as learning, coordinating movement and recognizing faces. These tasks all change connections in the brain, essentially undermining the platform that is set up for that learning. Sleep, Hengen contends, allows the brain to reset. According to this hypothesis, the restoration, which occurs through a common biological process known as homeostasis, is the ‘set point’ at which the brain is able to maximize information-processing potential
1
.
Hengen compares homeostasis to the familiar workings of a home heating system. A drop in a room’s temperature below the set point causes the heater to turn on, restoring the environment to the desired level of warmth.
Likewise, when the brain is further from its critical point, a person will feel more tired and need to fall asleep to reset. The closer the brain is to its critical point the more likely the person is to stay awake, because they will have plenty of capacity for doing and learning.
Sleep has several mechanisms that help the brain to reset after the stimulus and onslaught of information of each day. According to a 2024 study, parts of the hippocampus go silent during sleep, preparing its neurons for use again the next day
2
. And a 2017 study
3
found that, in the brains of mice, sleep restores the balance of junctions between neurons called synapses, which grow during the day and shrink during sleep.
Rogulja’s team confirmed that sleep is indeed important for homeostasis, but that the organ in which this takes place is not the brain.
After determining the ten-day timeline for sleep deprivation and death in flies, Vaccaro, who had previously studied sleep deprivation and ageing, began looking for markers of ageing in these insects. data.title: Controlling Language and Diffusion Models by Transporting Activations
data.author: 2bit
data.article_summary: 苹果公司研究人员开发了一种名为Activation Transport（AcT）的新技术，用于精细控制生成模型的输出。与依赖强化学习与人类反馈（RLHF）或指令微调的传统方法不同，AcT不改变模型参数，而是在推理时动态调整输出，避免了计算开销和性能影响。该方法利用最优传输理论，在源激活和目标激活分布之间建立映射，确保调整后的激活仍在模型训练期间学习的分布范围内，从而减少意外行为和性能下降。AcT提供了更可靠的结果，且无需大量数据和复杂计算，相比提示工程更具优势。该研究将在ICLR 2025上作为 spotlight 展示，代码已开放。

不同观点：

• [vessenes] 详细解释了一种通过“Optimal Transport Map”来移除特定概念的方法，并讨论了该方法的实现细节和潜在问题，比如是否类似于低秩适配器（LoRA）或平均差异的计算。
• [roro_7] 认为模型越智能越难控制，提出如果完全控制模型，可能会导致模型变得不智能，强调独立思考是智能模型的核心特性。
• [bradneuberg] 认为这项技术是一个重要的突破，提供了一种非RHLF（基于人类反馈的强化学习）机制来限制和聚焦深度网络。
• [imranq] 认为这实际上只是用一种复杂的方式描述LoRA，本质上仍是基于特定输出学习权重并应用于推理。

• [roro_7] 强调了模型智能与控制之间的权衡，暗示完全控制可能导致模型失去独立性和智能性，这是一个值得注意的讨论点。

Controlling Language and Diffusion Models by Transporting Activations
Large generative models are becoming increasingly capable and more widely deployed to power production applications, but getting these models to produce exactly what's desired can still be challenging. Fine-grained control over these models' outputs is important to meet user expectations and to mitigate potential misuses, ensuring the models' reliability and safety. To address these issues, Apple machine learning researchers have developed a new technique that is modality-agnostic and provides fine-grained control over the model's behavior with negligible computational overhead, while minimally impacting the model's abilities.
Activation Transport (AcT)
is a general framework to steer activations guided by optimal transport theory that generalizes many previous activation-steering works. The work will be presented as a Spotlight at
ICLR 2025
, and code is available
here
.
To help generative models produce output that aligns with their users' expectations, researchers often rely on reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF) or instruction fine-tuning, but these approaches are resource-intensive and become increasingly impractical as models grow in complexity. In addition, changing a model's parameters can have unintended consequences, affecting its overall performance on other tasks.
To control the output of these generative models, users often try crafting precise prompts, but while this is more accessible, it offers limited controls. Even with carefully constructed prompts, a modelâs output can be unpredictable and lacking the nuance a user might need. For example, itâs common for models to fail when prompted with instructions not to include something
(see figure 1)
:
Figure 1: Text-to-Image model such as SDXL and FLUX.1.dev tend to generate pink elephants even when instructed not to generate one. Left: âAn astronaut in a space station. Do not show a pink elephantâ. Right: âA dog running on the beach splashing water. Do not show a pink elephantâ.
In many applications, such as content generation, creative writing, or even AI-assisted design, having fine-grained control over the model's output is crucial. For example, a user might want to adjust the tone of text without altering its content, change the style of generated images while maintaining their context, or to ensure sensitive topics are handled with care, without compromising overall coherence. Activation Transport (AcT) delivers this, without the computational overhead, complexity, and volume of data required by RLHF or fine-tuning, and with more reliable results than prompt engineering.
Activation Steering: A simple-yet-powerful solution
The computational and economic cost of fine-tuning large models as well as the need for fine-grained control has motivated research on targeted interventions upon model activations to modify specific behaviors in a fine-grained way. The main advantage of these "activation steering" methods is that they do not require back-propagation and typically can be merged into the model weights.
Unlike RLHF or fine-tuning, activation steering doesn't impact a model's parameters, but instead leverages an understanding of the model's operations to dynamically steer its outputs in a desired direction at inference time.
Prior approaches to activation steering have used a vector-based intervention that take the source activations of expert neurons, and shift them toward a learned target
(see figure 2)
. However, the degree to which activations are shifted is controlled by an unbounded model-level parameter (Î»\lambda), making interpretable interventions challenging. Additionally, these interventions can shift activations out of distribution, meaning that the shifted activations can end up far from what the model has learned to expect during training, resulting in a disruption of the model's natural dynamics, which can lead to unexpected behavior and reduced performance.
Figure 2: Prior Activation Steering works using vector-based steering will likely move activations out of distribution. The intervention strength parameter Î» is unbounded and non-interpretable.
Activation Transport (AcT) and Linear-AcT
Activation Transport (AcT) is a novel intervention framework that surpasses the prior limitations of activation steering by accounting for distributions of source and target activations, and using an interpretable and actionable strength parameter for fine-grained control.
AcT learns the Optimal Transport (OT) map between the source and target activation distributions. This ensures that an activation transported from the source will comply with the target distribution, minimizing the compounding effects on the dynamics of the model itself. 43646466.article_summary: 苹果公司研究人员开发了一种名为Activation Transport（AcT）的新技术，用于精细控制生成模型的输出。与依赖强化学习与人类反馈（RLHF）或指令微调的传统方法不同，AcT不改变模型参数，而是在推理时动态调整输出，避免了计算开销和性能影响。该方法利用最优传输理论，在源激活和目标激活分布之间建立映射，确保调整后的激活仍在模型训练期间学习的分布范围内，从而减少意外行为和性能下降。AcT提供了更可靠的结果，且无需大量数据和复杂计算，相比提示工程更具优势。该研究将在ICLR 2025上作为 spotlight 展示，代码已开放。
43646466.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于多模态LLM（大型语言模型）的控制与优化方案的讨论，尤其是如何有效移除或控制特定概念（如“粉色大象”），以及相关技术（如LoRA、Optimal Transport Map）的实现和应用。

不同观点：
• [scorps] 认为人类在处理“不要想粉色大象”这样的问题上存在共性，暗示控制某些特定概念的难度。
• [sampton] 提出多模态LLM是真正的解决方案，但苹果公司可能在寻找能在当前设备上运行的方案，强调设备本地运行的需求。
• [vessenes] 详细解释了一种通过“Optimal Transport Map”来移除特定概念的方法，并讨论了该方法的实现细节和潜在问题，比如是否类似于低秩适配器（LoRA）或平均差异的计算。
• [roro_7] 认为模型越智能越难控制，提出如果完全控制模型，可能会导致模型变得不智能，强调独立思考是智能模型的核心特性。
• [bradneuberg] 认为这项技术是一个重要的突破，提供了一种非RHLF（基于人类反馈的强化学习）机制来限制和聚焦深度网络。
• [imranq] 认为这实际上只是用一种复杂的方式描述LoRA，本质上仍是基于特定输出学习权重并应用于推理。
• [turnsout] 对苹果公司严格控制输出的兴趣表示理解，并猜测这项工作是否已经应用于Image Playground。

补充讨论：
• 关于“Optimal Transport Map”的具体实现存在争议，[vessenes] 和 [imranq] 都提到了它是否与LoRA或简单的权重调整类似，但未达成一致。
• [roro_7] 强调了模型智能与控制之间的权衡，暗示完全控制可能导致模型失去独立性和智能性，这是一个值得注意的讨论点。

不同观点：
• ebri认为R的data.table包比Python的pandas强大得多，甚至tidyverse也比pandas好。他表达了对R的怀念，尤其在研究工作中，R的效率更高。

• brcmthrowaway询问R是否支持LLM（大语言模型）。

1
Your last-ever bookmark
Thanks for stopping by. If you’re like me, you can’t help but bookmark every R-related programming book you find in the hopes that one day you, or someone you know, might find it useful.
Hopefully this is the only bookmark you’ll need in future ;).
When I initially released this collection in late August 2020, it contained about 100 books that I’d been collecting over the previous two years. Since then I’ve found a few more and there have been contributions from many people. The collection now stands at over 400 free, open-sourced books.
Most of these are free. Some are paid but usually quite affordable.
1.1
Searching
If there’s something specific you’re looking for, use the menu or search using the magnifying glass icon at the top of the screen.
1.2
Supporting
If you’d like to show your appreciation with a donation you’re most welcome to do so here:
1.3
Contributing
Please feel free to contribute paid and free books - see
GitHub.
or submit via the
Google Form
.
1.4
Big thanks to Fathom Data
I want to give a special thanks to the folks at
Fathom Data
who converted the site from bookdown to Quarto. I’ve worked with Fathom Data for many years and can highly recommend their services!
1.5
License
This website/book is free to use, and is licensed under the
Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivs 3.0 License
.
1.6
Live stats
Who says you can’t have privacy AND transparency??
I’m guessing that if you’re interested in R then you also like data ;).
Note that “unique” visits will be higher in Plausible than you’d find with Google Analytics. Because Plausible is GDPR compliant and privacy focused, each user is identified for only 1 day. If someone visits the site 2 days in a row, that’s counted as 2 “uniques” whereas in Google Analytics it would only be counted as 1 unique visitor because of the presence of persistent cookies and such that allows for tracking of users.
From now on, you can view the
LIVE site stats right here
.
1.7
About me
I’m Oscar. If you like this book, feel free to say “Hi!” on
Mastodon
or
LinkedIn
.
If you want to stay in the loop on other data-related products I create, or major updates to this book, sign up to my
newsletter
.

data.title: Usability Improvements in GCC 15
data.author: dmalcolm
data.article_summary:
文章总结了GCC 15编译器在可用性方面的六项改进，重点介绍了诊断信息的美观性和易读性提升。主要内容包括：

1. **更美观的执行路径**：通过添加警告表情符号（⚠️）和ASCII艺术展示控制流，帮助用户更直观地理解代码问题。
2. **C++模板错误的新外观**：简化和重构C++模板错误信息，使其更易读。例如，将原先GCC 14中长达34行的错误信息进行优化，使其更简洁。

其他改进还包括对诊断信息中Unicode字符的使用、减少视觉噪音等，旨在提升开发者的使用体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GCC编译器错误信息显示的改进及相关功能讨论

不同观点：
• [mwkaufma] 认为不应劫持浏览器的后退按钮，这属于可用性改进请求。
• [munificent] 赞赏通过层次结构展示模板错误，认为这种方法很聪明，并解释了在处理C++模板时遇到的复杂错误树问题，支持这种展示方式。
• [porphyra] 支持新的嵌套错误信息显示方式，认为这使得阅读错误信息更加容易，只需关注顶层缩进即可。
• [jmclnx] 希望GCC由于GPL继续成为Linux的默认编译器，但预计未来clang可能会取代它，并对GCC合并COBOL支持表示赞赏。
• [codeshaunted] 支持所有改进，但不喜欢控制台中出现表情符号。
• [bmn__] 引用David Malcolm的文章，批评C标准的版本控制方法，认为代码的版本应伴随代码本身，而不是通过编译器调用指定。
• [levodelellis] 希望有一个配置文件或环境变量来简化错误信息显示，只关注行号和唯一错误信息，并希望能够扩展错误信息。
• [meisel] 认为模板错误信息显示很好，并建议为clang和旧版GCC用户编写错误信息转换器。
• [Night_Thastus] 支持更好的错误信息显示，但由于环境限制无法使用Clang，期待GCC的改进能在MSYS中看到。
• [kazinator] 认为GCC 3.4.6已经非常易用，新的华丽诊断功能是多余的，并将其比作洛可可时期的装饰艺术，认为这些功能虽然有趣但不必要。
• [jart] 提供了GCC 15的发布说明链接，并对一些新的优化和功能提出疑问和建议，如__builtin_stdc_rotate_left()的必要性等。
• [taschenorakel] 认为Unicode艺术是浪费，建议将精力放在帮助IDE理解错误信息上，认为这更有用。
• [wiseowise] 对控制台中出现警告表情符号表示不满，调侃下一步是否会用表情符号表示错误。
• [brcmthrowaway] 询问GCC插件的状态。
• [budmichstelk] 赞赏GCC的现代化努力，认为许多旧问题已经解决，并带来了许多新的改进。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于新的错误信息显示方式是否必要和有用。一部分用户认为新的层次结构展示和Unicode艺术是改进，而另一部分用户认为这些是多余的装饰，简洁的错误信息更重要。
• 用户对表情符号的使用存在分歧，一部分用户不喜欢控制台中出现表情符号，认为这是不必要的装饰。
• 对GCC未来发展和功能改进方向的建议和期待，包括对GCC插件状态的询问和对具体新功能的疑问。

43643886.article_content:
6 usability improvements in GCC 15
April 10, 2025
David Malcolm
Related topics:
C
C++
Compilers
Linux
Secure Coding
Related products:
Red Hat Enterprise Linux
Share:
Table of contents:
I work at Red Hat on
GCC, the GNU Compiler Collection
. I spent most of the past year working on how GCC emits diagnostics (errors and warnings) in the hope of making it easier to use. Let's take a look at 6 improvements to look forward to in the upcoming GCC 15.
1. Prettier execution paths
I added a
static analyzer to GCC in GCC 10
that prints visualizations of predicted paths of execution through the user's code, demonstrating each problem it predicts.
Here's an example that shows some of the improvements I've made to this in GCC 15:
infinite-loop-linked-list.c: In function ‘while_loop_missing_next’:
infinite-loop-linked-list.c:30:10: warning: infinite loop [CWE-835] [-Wanalyzer-infinite-loop]
30 |   while (n)
|          ^
‘while_loop_missing_next’: events 1-3
30 |   while (n)
|          ^
|          |
|          (1) ⚠️  infinite loop here
|          (2) when ‘n’ is non-NULL: always following ‘true’ branch... ─>─┐
|                                                                         │
|                                                                         │
|┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
31 |│    {
32 |│      sum += n->val;
|│             ~~~~~~
|│              |
|└─────────────>(3) ...to here
‘while_loop_missing_next’: event 4
32 |       sum += n->val;
|       ~~~~^~~~~~~~~
|           |
|           (4) looping back... ─>─┐
|                                  │
‘while_loop_missing_next’: event 5
|                                  │
|┌─────────────────────────────────┘
30 |│  while (n)
|│         ^
|│         |
|└────────>(5) ...to here
I've added a warning emoji (⚠️) to the event in the path where the problem occurs (event 1 in the above), and I've added "ASCII art" to show control flow, such as the lines connecting events 2 and 3, and those connecting events 4 and 5 (compare with the
GCC 14 output seen here
).
Another example of an execution path can be seen in this new
-fanalyzer
warning
-Wanalyzer-undefined-behavior-ptrdiff
, which warns about pointer subtractions involving different chunks of memory:
demo.c: In function ‘test_invalid_calc_of_array_size’:
demo.c:9:20: warning: undefined behavior when subtracting pointers [CWE-469] [-Wanalyzer-undefined-behavior-ptrdiff]
9 |   return &sentinel - arr;
|                    ^
events 1-2
│
│    3 | int arr[42];
│      |     ~~~
│      |     |
│      |     (2) underlying object for right-hand side of subtraction created here
│    4 | int sentinel;
│      |     ^~~~~~~~
│      |     |
│      |     (1) underlying object for left-hand side of subtraction created here
│
└──> ‘test_invalid_calc_of_array_size’: event 3
│
│    9 |   return &sentinel - arr;
│      |                    ^
│      |                    |
│      |                    (3) ⚠️  subtraction of pointers has undefined behavior if they do not point into the same array object
│
There's a line on the left-hand side that visualizes the stack depth to highlight calls and returns.  As of GCC 15 this now uses unicode box-drawing characters (where the locale supports this), and for purely intraprocedual cases like the
-Wanalyzer-infinite-loop
example above, we now omit it altogether, which saves some visual "noise."
2. A new look for C++ template errors
Compiler errors involving C++ templates are notoriously difficult to read.
Consider this invalid C++ code:
struct widget {};
void draw (widget &);
struct diagram {};
void draw (diagram &);
template <class W>
concept drawable = requires(W w) { w.draw (); };
template <drawable T>
void draw(T);
int main ()
{
draw (widget ());
}
Attempting to
compile it with GCC 14
with
-fconcepts -fconcepts-diagnostics-depth=2
gives 34 lines of output, which is relatively simple as far as these go, and even this can be hard to decipher. I'll post it here for reference, but I confess that my eyes tend to glaze over when I try to read it:
<source>: In function 'int main()':
<source>:15:8: error: no matching function for call to 'draw(widget)'
15 |   draw (widget ());
|   ~~~~~^~~~~~~~~~~
<source>:2:6: note: candidate: 'void draw(widget&)' (near match)
2 | void draw (widget &);
|      ^~~~
<source>:2:6: note:   conversion of argument 1 would be ill-formed:
<source>:15:9: error: cannot bind non-const lvalue reference of type 'widget&' to an rvalue of type 'widget'
15 |   draw (widget ());
|         ^~~~~~~~~
<source>:5:6: note: candidate: 'void draw(diagram&)'
5 | void draw (diagram &);
|      ^~~~
<source>:5:12: note:   no known conversion for argument 1 from 'widget' to 'diagram&'
5 | void draw (diagram &);
|            ^~~~~~~~~
<source>:11:6: note: candidate: 'template<class T>  requires  drawable<T> void draw(T)'
11 | void draw(T);
|      ^~~~
<source>:11:6: note:   template argument deduction/substitution failed:
<source>:11:6: note: constr

1. **更美观的执行路径**：通过添加警告表情符号（⚠️）和ASCII艺术展示控制流，帮助用户更直观地理解代码问题。
2. **C++模板错误的新外观**：简化和重构C++模板错误信息，使其更易读。例如，将原先GCC 14中长达34行的错误信息进行优化，使其更简洁。

其他改进还包括对诊断信息中Unicode字符的使用、减少视觉噪音等，旨在提升开发者的使用体验。

data.title: Garfield Minus Garfield
data.author: mike1o1
data.article_summary: "Garfield Minus Garfield"是一个网站，专门将《加菲猫》漫画中的加菲猫角色移除，以展现主角乔恩·阿布库的内心困境。这使得漫画变成了一种对孤独和抑郁的深刻探索，反映了乔恩在一个安静的美国郊区的孤独生活。网站由丹·沃尔什创建，通过社交媒体和RSS提供更新，并托管在Tumblr上。该项目还提供了档案和常见问题解答，并公开了原作者的看法和网站的Twitter动态。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“Garfield Minus Garfield”项目的各种观点和讨论

不同观点：
• [nickvec] 认为“Garfield Minus Garfield”揭示了Jon Arbuckle的孤独与抑郁，使读者在某种程度上产生共鸣。这个评论强调了对Jon存在主义焦虑的解读。
• [grepLeigh] 提到了该项目的多年前互联网背景（通过Stumbleupon发现），并对该项目至今仍然存在表示欣喜。
• [jf] 指出该项目得到了原作者Jim Davis的认可，并且还出版了官方书籍，强调了该项目在主流文化中的合法性。
• [dimal] 怀念早年互联网上充斥着像“Garfield Minus Garfield”这样搞笑内容的时代，而不是现在算法优化的社交媒体内容。
• [jsheard] 认为“Garfield Minus Garfield”不错，但“Lasagna Cat”更上一层楼，提供了另一种与Garfield相关的创作形式。
• [noman-land] 提出了一种类似的新项目创意，希望看到移除主持人后的播客版本（如“Rogan Minus Rogan”），以探索新的内容形式。
• [yoyohello13] 将“Garfield Minus Garfield”解读为一种心理恐怖，并引用了Super Eyepatch Wolf的分析视频，强调了该项目在恐怖题材中的潜力。
• [AdmiralAsshat] 认为流行的解读忽略了“Garfield Minus Garfield”中Jon找到平凡乐趣的一面，指出该项目并不总是 depressing。
• [throwme0827349] 表达了对“Garfield Minus Garfield”的喜爱，并将其与“Nietzsche Family Circus”相比较，认为两者都有幽默且深刻的特质，但后者未获得同样的关注。
• [jonathaneunice] 认为该项目比他想象的更加黑暗。

补充讨论：
• [qingcharles] 提供了其他相关的网络链接，如“GarfieldMinusJon”和“AlzheimersGroup”，扩展了讨论的范围，提供了更多类似内容。
• [windowshopping] 对网站上漫画日期的混乱表示困惑，提出了关于日期显示和内容顺序的问题。
• [HeliumHydride] 提供了另一个与“Garfield Minus Garfield”相关的项目链接，即“the square root of minus Garfield”，为讨论增加了新维度。
• [brailsafe] 提到点击某个帖子后进入了不当内容的404页面，提醒其他用户注意，并表达了对这种现象的不满。

争议焦点：
• 项目的性质：有人认为该项目揭示了Jon的孤独和抑郁（如[nickvec]），而另一些人则认为它展现了Jon找到平凡乐趣的一面（如[AdmiralAsshat]）。
• 日期混乱：[windowshopping] 对网站日期的随机性表示困惑，提出了技术上的问题。
• 不当内容：[brailsafe] 提到网站链接到了不当内容，提出了对用户体验和网站管理的担忧。

data.title: A surprising enum size optimization in the Rust compiler
data.author: returningfory2
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了Rust编译器对枚举类型内存表示的优化。枚举类型由多个变体组成，每个变体可以有不同的数据 payload。通常，枚举的大小是最大变体的大小加上用于标识变体的标签（tag）的大小。文章详细解释了如何通过打印内存表示来观察这些标签和数据。

文章还介绍了“niche 优化”，这是一种针对只有一个变体带有 payload 的枚举的优化。例如，`Option<char>` 枚举通过利用无效的 char 值来表示 `None`，从而无需额外的标签字节。

文章最后提到了一种新的优化发现，涉及嵌套枚举。例如，嵌套的 `Inner` 枚举按预期占用 8 字节，但通过进一步优化，Rust 编译器能够更有效地表示这些嵌套结构。这种优化超出了已知的 niche 优化，展示了 Rust 编译器在处理复杂枚举时的智能优化策略。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust中无效UTF-8字符引发未定义行为的原因及相关内存优化技术（如niche optimization）的讨论。

不同观点：
• **[mmastrac]** 认为，Rust中的`char`是一个特殊的整数类型，具有有效的取值范围，如果构造了无效的`char`，可能会绕过niche optimization，导致不健全的转换（unsound transmute），从而破坏代码的健全性（soundness）。他还提到了其他类似行为的类型，如`NonZero<...>`。

• **[pitaj]** 不同意mmastrac对niche optimization的理解，指出这是niche优化的实际应用，外部枚举利用了内部枚举标签中的空位（niches）作为自己的判别值（discriminant）。

• **[packetlost]** 认为问题可能不是"扁平化"枚举的判别空间，而是32位对齐要求加上子字节判别大小的问题。他指出，枚举变体的顺序不匹配可能与编译器的填充和对其要求有关，并且提到嵌套的`match`语句可以被理论上扁平化为跳转表。

• **[ComputerGuru]** 提出了一种更激进的嵌套枚举优化方案，即自动重新分配枚举值以避免冲突，从而实现无标签区分。虽然这种优化是可行的，但社区认为这是一个较大的需求，可能需要更严格的限制版本才能实现。

• **[Joker_vD]** 引用了SML/NJ编译器的相关内容，指出压缩枚举的技巧在ML等语言中也有类似应用，但这些技巧通常只适用于模块内部的未导出数据类型，因为数据类型可以是抽象的。

• **[kazinator]** 将问题总结为"标签合并"（tag merging），即当一个枚举的成员是另一个枚举时，两者可以有效合并为一个判别标签，但需要重新编号以避免重叠。

• **[subarctic]** 提到过去需要手动扁平化嵌套枚举以节省空间，质疑这种优化是何时实现的。

• **[lordnacho]** 询问niche optimization是否要求编译器对类型有特殊了解，以及如何实现一个更高级的内存布局可视化工具，能够识别指针。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中多次提到niche optimization及其应用和限制。
- 提到了Rust编译器的优化能力以及内存布局对齐和填充的影响。
- 有人关注如何进一步改进和自动化枚举的优化，特别是嵌套枚举的内存布局优化。

A surprising enum size optimization in the Rust compiler
April 7, 2025
Enums are one of the most popular features in Rust.
An enum is type whose value is one of a specified set of variants.
/// Foo is either a 32-bit integer or character.
enum Foo {
Int(u32),
Char(char),
}
Values of type
Foo
are either
integers (e.g. the variant
Foo::Int(3)
with a payload of
3
)
or characters (e.g. the variant
Foo::Char('A')
with a payload of
'A'
).
If you think of structs as being the
and
combination of their fields,
enums are the
or
combination of their variants.
This post is about a surprising optimization that the Rust compiler
performs on the memory representation of enum values
in order to make their memory usage smaller
(spoiler: it’s not the niche optimization).
In general, keeping values small can result in faster programs because values get passed
around in CPU registers and more values fit in single CPU cache lines.
Generally the size of an enum is the size of the largest payload,
plus some extra bytes for storing a
tag
that specifies which variant the value is.
For the type
Foo
above, both variant payloads take up 4 bytes,
and we need an additional byte at least for the tag.
A requirement called “type alignment” (which I won’t get into)
requires that Rust actually use 4 bytes for the tag.
So the overall size of the type is 8 bytes:
assert_eq!(std::mem::size_of::<Foo>(), 8);
(All the code snippets can be run
here in the Rust Playground
.)
For the rest of this article it will be useful and interesting to actually see the memory
representation of various enum values.
Here’s a function that prints the raw bytes representation of any Rust value:
/// Print the memory representation of a value of a type T.
fn print_memory_representation<T: std::fmt::Debug>(t: T) {
print!("type={} value={t:?}: ", std::any::type_name::<T>());
let start = &t as *const _ as *const u8;
for i in 0..std::mem::size_of::<T>() {
print!("{:02x} ", unsafe {*start.offset(i as isize)});
}
println!();
}
(This function was adapted from this
10-year old Reddit post
.)
Let’s run this for our enum
Foo
.
print_memory_representation(Foo::Int(5));
// type=Foo value=Int(5): 00 00 00 00 05 00 00 00
//                        |-- tag --| |- value -|
print_memory_representation(Foo::Char('A'));
// type=Foo value=Char('A'): 01 00 00 00 41 00 00 00
//                           |-- tag --| |- value -|
The first thing to point out is that this computer’s memory is
little endian
,
so the lowest bytes come first.
In 32-bit hex the number 5 is
0x00000005
, but its little endian representation is
05 00 00 00
.
With that in mind, we see that the first 4 bytes are the tag.
The integer variant has been assigned tag 0,
and the character variant tag 1.
The second 4 bytes are then just the usual values of the payload.
Note that the lowercase letter “a” is 41 in ASCII,
which is why its memory representation is
41 00 00 00
.
The niche optimization
Aside from the general tags scheme,
there is one well known enum size optimization called the niche optimization.
This optimization works for types where only one of the variants has a payload.
A good example is the built in option type:
enum Option<char> {
None,
Some(char),
}
Based on the tags analysis in the last section we might guess the enum size will be 8 bytes
(the largest payload of 4 bytes plus 4 bytes for the tag).
But actually values of this type only use 4 bytes of memory in total:
assert_eq!(std::mem::size_of::<Option<char>>(), 4);
What’s going on?
The Rust compiler knows that while
char
takes up 4 bytes of memory,
not every value of those 4 bytes is a valid value of
char
.
Char only has about
2^21
valid values (one for each Unicode code point),
whereas 4 bytes support
2^32
different values.
The compiler choses one of these invalid bit patterns as a
niche
.
It then represents the enum value without using tags.
It represents the
Some
variant identically to char.
It represents the
None
variant using the niche.
One interesting question is: what exact niche does Rust use?
Let’s print the memory representations to see:
let a: char = 'A'
print_memory_representation(a);
// type=char value='A': 41 00 00 00
print_memory_representation(Some(a));
// type=Option<char> value=Some('A'): 41 00 00 00
let none: Option<char> = None;
print_memory_representation(none);
// type=Option<char> value=None: 00 00 11 00
As we see, the memory representations of
'A'
and
Some('A')
are identical.
Rust represents
None
using the 32-bit number
0x00110000
.
A quick search reveals that this number is exactly one bigger than the largest
valid Unicode code point.
Beyond the niche optimization?
My understanding was that Rust doesn’t perform any more optimizations,
so I was pleasantly surprised recently when I found one.
The context is nested enums. Start with an inner enum
enum Inner {
A(u32),
B(u32),
}
If we look at the representation in memory,
it’s as we expect: 8 bytes, where the first 4 bytes store the tag
and the last 4

• **[mmastrac]** 认为，Rust中的`char`是一个特殊的整数类型，具有有效的取值范围，如果构造了无效的`char`，可能会绕过niche optimization，导致不健全的转换（unsound transmute），从而破坏代码的健全性（soundness）。他还提到了其他类似行为的类型，如`NonZero<...>`。

• **[pitaj]** 不同意mmastrac对niche optimization的理解，指出这是niche优化的实际应用，外部枚举利用了内部枚举标签中的空位（niches）作为自己的判别值（discriminant）。

• **[packetlost]** 认为问题可能不是"扁平化"枚举的判别空间，而是32位对齐要求加上子字节判别大小的问题。他指出，枚举变体的顺序不匹配可能与编译器的填充和对其要求有关，并且提到嵌套的`match`语句可以被理论上扁平化为跳转表。

• **[ComputerGuru]** 提出了一种更激进的嵌套枚举优化方案，即自动重新分配枚举值以避免冲突，从而实现无标签区分。虽然这种优化是可行的，但社区认为这是一个较大的需求，可能需要更严格的限制版本才能实现。

• **[Joker_vD]** 引用了SML/NJ编译器的相关内容，指出压缩枚举的技巧在ML等语言中也有类似应用，但这些技巧通常只适用于模块内部的未导出数据类型，因为数据类型可以是抽象的。

• **[kazinator]** 将问题总结为"标签合并"（tag merging），即当一个枚举的成员是另一个枚举时，两者可以有效合并为一个判别标签，但需要重新编号以避免重叠。

• **[subarctic]** 提到过去需要手动扁平化嵌套枚举以节省空间，质疑这种优化是何时实现的。

• **[lordnacho]** 询问niche optimization是否要求编译器对类型有特殊了解，以及如何实现一个更高级的内存布局可视化工具，能够识别指针。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中多次提到niche optimization及其应用和限制。
- 提到了Rust编译器的优化能力以及内存布局对齐和填充的影响。
- 有人关注如何进一步改进和自动化枚举的优化，特别是嵌套枚举的内存布局优化。

data.title: Show HN: Koreo – A platform engineering toolkit for Kubernetes
data.author: tylertreat
data.article_summary: Koreo 是一个用于 Kubernetes 配置管理和资源编排的新工具包，通过可编程工作流和结构化数据增强开发者能力。它支持定义复杂的多步骤工作流，自动化从简单部署到整个云环境的流程，并允许将配置分解为可重用的函数以促进模块化和减少重复。Koreo 采用声明式操作模型，自动协调实际状态以匹配期望状态，简化管理并确保基础设施一致性。它提供一流的测试和工具支持，将配置视为代码，帮助提前发现错误。通过配置层、可插入逻辑和动态资源具象化，Koreo 帮助开发者聚焦产品开发，而非基础设施复杂性，并支持构建自助服务平台和自动化环境创建。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Koreo项目的评价与争议

不同观点：
• **支持与鼓励**：

  - [debschillin] 对Koreo简化复杂工作流的概念表示兴奋，特别是将K8s组件视为“乐高”的想法。

  - [clvx] 提到已经使用FluxCD和Cuelang构建了类似系统，并认为FluxCD需要一个与CLI功能匹配的UI。
  - [hbogert] 提到Timoni并询问Koreo的比较优势。

• **对YAML的批评**：
  - [peterldowns] 以讽刺的方式表达了对YAML泛滥的不满。
  - [nikolayasdf123] 质疑K8s生态系统中YAML和配置文件的繁多，并希望减少YAML和配置。
  - [nosefrog] 分享了使用Python生成配置的经验，并提到在Google工作时使用gcl（KCL和Jsonnet的前身）导致的噩梦和许多故障。

• **功能与实用性讨论**：
  - [Esras] 认为Koreo与Argo Workflows和Argo CD有重叠，但需要更清晰的理解和区分。

• **技术选择与替代方案**：
  - [dlahoda] 认为YAML不适合，并建议使用逐渐类型化的语言如Nickel。

- 争议的焦点在于YAML的泛滥和Kubernetes的复杂性，用户对新工具的需求和期望，以及Koreo相对于其他工具的独特优势。
- 用户对Koreo的实际应用和开发体验存在困惑，特别是与现有系统和工具的比较以及如何更好地理解其价值。

The
platform engineering toolkit
for Kubernetes
Koreo is a new approach to
Kubernetes configuration management and resource orchestration
empowering developers through programmable workflows and structured data
Get Started
Learn More
Programmable workflows
Define complex, multi-step processes that react to events and manage the lifecycle of your Kubernetes resources. Koreo workflows enable automation of everything from simple deployments to entire cloud environments. It's like programmingâor
choreographing
âKubernetes controllers.
Structured configuration management
Manage Kubernetes configurations the way they were intendedâas structured data, not just templated strings. This allows you to easily validate, transform, and combine configurations from multiple sources in a manageable and scalable way.
Dynamic resource materialization
Inject values from a config file or overlay partial definitions to build up a complete resource view. Combine configurations from different sources like security, compliance, and SRE, and even apply custom logic, to give developers a golden path for provisioning applications, resources, or anything Kubernetes manages.
Configuration as functions
Inspired by functional programming principles, Koreo lets you decompose configuration into functions. These functions act as reusable building blocks to encapsulate common tasks and logic within your Koreo workflows. This promotes modularity, reduces duplication, and makes workflows easier to maintain and evolve.
Declarative operator model
Define your desired state through workflows and functions, and Koreo will automatically reconcile the actual state to match. This declarative approach simplifies management and ensures consistency across your infrastructure.
First-class testing and tooling
Actually
treat configuration as code with Koreo's built-in testing framework and developer tooling. Write unit tests for individual functions and entire workflows to catch errors early and prevent unexpected behavior. Koreo's IDE integration gives you real-time feedback, autocomplete, and introspection.
Powerful configuration management
with flexible resource orchestration
Koreo is a platform engineering toolkit that introduces a new approach to configuration management and resource orchestration in Kubernetes. It builds upon the best aspects of tools like Helm, Kustomize, Argo, and Crossplane while addressing some of their limitations.
It serves as a meta-controller programming language and runtime
that allows you to compose off-the-shelf operators into cohesive platforms by orchestrating Kubernetes controllers. Through powerful primitives, Koreo enables DevOps and platform engineers to create dynamic workflows that automate everything from simple deployments to entire internal developer platforms. Its layered configuration management enables teams like security, compliance, or SRE to enforce consistent standards and practices for resources within your organization.
Workflows and functions
provide composable primitives for building platforms
Koreo empowers you to build complex Kubernetes platforms using composable workflows and functions
, drawing inspiration from functional programming principles. Workflows act as blueprints for platform operations, defining the steps for tasks like application deployments or infrastructure provisioning. Functions are the individual building blocks within these workflows, encapsulating specific logic for data transformation, API interaction, or resource creation. And with built-in testing, you can validate configuration and catch errors early in the development process.
The true power of Koreo lies in its ability to program these workflows. Incorporate conditional logic, loops, and error handling to create dynamic platform operations. Automate complex processes, enforce policies, and build self-service platforms for your development teams.

data.title: Why Tap a Wheel of Cheese?
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了帕尔马干酪（Parmigiano Reggiano）质量检测的独特过程，由一支24人的专业团队"battitori"负责。他们使用小金属锤敲击奶酪轮，通过声音在6-7秒内判断是否存在缺陷。文章跟随了两位battitori——37岁的Alessandro Stocchi和他81岁的导师Renato Giudici，展示了这一传统技艺的传承。检测时，奶酪轮被置于凳子上以避免杂音，通过敲击声判断内部结构是否 compact。奶酪被分为三个等级：最高质量适合长期陈化、次级质量建议尽早食用、有明显缺陷的作为普通餐桌奶酪。尽管有些缺陷是自然的产物，但整体瑕疵率很低。这一工作需要极大的热情和谦逊，且技艺通过实践代代相传。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：意大利传统奶酪制作工艺，特别是Parmigiano Reggiano的手工与技术应用之间的平衡。

不同观点：
• [SamBam] 认为虽然技术上可以通过机器检测奶酪的空洞或密度不均，但保留手工制作的传统能避免工业化生产导致质量下降。手工制作更多是与传统感觉相关，而非实际影响产品质量。
• [ziofill] 强调作为意大利人，Parmigiano Reggiano和Grana Padano是最好的奶酪，不仅可以用于意面，还可以单独食用或搭配其他食物，凸显了其多功能性和文化意义。
• [nancyminusone] 观察到在奶酪生产中已经部分引入了技术，比如电动搅拌和机器人翻转奶酪轮，但仍有人工参与。讨论了技术与手工之间的平衡，并质疑何时应完全依赖技术或手工。
• [Uzmanali] 对检测奶酪缺陷的技能表示赞赏，认为这是独特的手工艺，体现了人工检测的非凡价值。
• [paulorlando] 对生产过程中变化的认知提出疑问，认为经过50年的经验积累，应该能够看到一致的结果，但事实似乎并非如此。
• [jacobgkau] 对不同质量的奶酪销售方式感兴趣，指出根据质量不同，奶酪会以不同品牌或无品牌形式出售，强调了质量分级的重要性。
• [dfxm12] 关注奶酪生产中的人为因素，质疑是否存在偏袒，并询问消费者是否会选择特定生产商的Parmigiano Reggiano。
• [saltcured] 提到一个可能的故事，关于人类专家通过嗅觉而非听觉判断奶酪质量，质疑检测技术的实际依据。
• [fracus] 认为手工检测似乎比看起来简单，只需要通过敲击判断是否中空，质疑手工技能的复杂性。
• [verelo] 通过个人故事分享了意大利文化中的“piano piano”（慢慢来）概念，表达了对传统价值观的喜爱。
• [taxicabjesus] 分享了因食用工业化奶酪导致健康问题的经历，强调了传统制作方法的重要性，特别是避免工业添加剂的使用。

补充讨论：
• 手工制作与技术应用之间的争议是主要焦点，部分评论者认为手工代表了传统和文化价值，而另一些人则认为技术能提高效率且不影响质量。
• 对奶酪质量的判断标准和销售方式也有较多讨论，尤其是如何通过品牌和质量分级来区分不同产品。
• 文化背景和个人经历影响了对奶酪制作工艺的看法，部分评论者从个人经验出发，强调了传统奶酪的独特性和健康益处。

43644970.article_content:
Why Tap a Wheel of Cheese?
Renato Giudici demonstrates his skill photo credit Kristine Jannuzzi
Behind the approximately 4 million wheels of Parmigiano Reggiano produced annually, there is a tiny team of 24 battitori responsible for ensuring the quality of each one. Armed with a small metal hammer, these specialized “drummers” tap every wheel after the minimum aging period of 12 months, and within 6-7 seconds they can detect if there are any defects, based purely on the sounds they hear.
Shadowing the Battitori
Author Kristine Jannuzzi with Alessandro Stocchi and Renato Giudici
I had the privilege of spending the morning with two of these maestros on the job in Emilia-Romagna: Alessandro Stocchi, a dynamic 37-year-old native of Reggio Emilia who began training to become a battitore in 2014, and his mentor, Renato Giudici, who at 81 years old, embodies a lifetime of passion for Parmigiano Reggiano. Renato is a former cheesemaker who made Parmigiano Reggiano for many years, and rather than retire, he chose to become a guardian of the King of Cheeses as a
battitore.
There’s no course to learn the niche skills and nuances of this trade; Alessandro accompanied and apprenticed with Renato and other experts for about 3 years, learning through firsthand experience how to assess each wheel.
“The particularity of this profession to me is that it’s like it was 200 years ago, and it’s a skill that’s handed down from generation to generation. You go around with the most expert, most experienced battitori, and you watch and listen to them, and slowly they start to give you the hammer. You try with them next to you, piano piano, and gradually, you begin to do more on your own,” explained Stocchi. “It’s a big responsibility, you have to be really capable of doing it, you can’t damage the cheese.”
How Parmigiano Reggiano is Evaluated
Alessandro Stocchi explains the grading system photo credit Kristine Jannuzzi
Renato showed me the ideal setup, with a wheel of Parmigiano Reggiano flat on a stool underneath the one that is being evaluated, so there is no extraneous noise. If the sound is homogeneous throughout the tapping, there are no defects.
“We hit all of the surfaces of the cheese, and from the sound of the hammer against the surface we can imagine in our mind an Xray of the wheel and how it is internally. For a perfect wheel with no defects, the paste is completely compact, no empty space. If there are structural defects, such as little fissures or cavities, we can hear that the sound of the hammer is different,” explained Stocchi.
Parmigiano Reggiano Categories
A cheese wheel with double parallel lines photo credit Kristine Jannuzzi
 Top quality, suitable for longer aging
 Lower quality, best consumed young
 Significant defects, not labeled Parmigiano Reggiano
There are three different categories to which the wheels are assigned. The first is perfect, or with negligible defects, and these wheels receive the fire-branded Parmigiano Reggiano mark. The second category with minor defects is still marked Parmigiano Reggiano, but the rind is engraved with parallel lines to indicate to the consumer that this is not the highest level, and probably best consumed young. And the third category is for wheels with more significant flaws, and the rind and all identifying marks are removed, so the cheese is sold as generic table cheese.
Renato Giudici taps a wheel photo credit Kristine Jannuzzi
“Sometimes when I do events and find a defect while I’m tapping a wheel, people who are watching turn their noses up. But to me it’s a beautiful thing that there are defects, and I’m not just saying it because if there aren’t any, I lose my job,” says Stocchi, laughing. “But the fact that there are defects indicates even more the artisanal quality of our product—we work with raw milk, without preservatives, each year there are many variations. Anyone who works with something in nature knows that not everything always goes how we would want or expect. I always say the day when we have 100% perfect Parmigiano Reggiano, we’d have to ask ourselves some questions, because it’s not an industrial product, so it’s normal that sometimes there are flaws.”
The number of wheels with defects remains low; in recent years, approximately 10% fell into the second category, and only about 1.5% were classified as third category.
“To do this job requires great passion, respect, and humility. My elder colleagues tell me you never stop learning, even after 50 years of doing it,” recounted Stocchi. “The day you think you’ve learned everything is the day you’ll start making errors.”

主要讨论点：意大利传统奶酪制作工艺，特别是Parmigiano Reggiano的手工与技术应用之间的平衡。

不同观点：
• [SamBam] 认为虽然技术上可以通过机器检测奶酪的空洞或密度不均，但保留手工制作的传统能避免工业化生产导致质量下降。手工制作更多是与传统感觉相关，而非实际影响产品质量。
• [ziofill] 强调作为意大利人，Parmigiano Reggiano和Grana Padano是最好的奶酪，不仅可以用于意面，还可以单独食用或搭配其他食物，凸显了其多功能性和文化意义。
• [nancyminusone] 观察到在奶酪生产中已经部分引入了技术，比如电动搅拌和机器人翻转奶酪轮，但仍有人工参与。讨论了技术与手工之间的平衡，并质疑何时应完全依赖技术或手工。
• [Uzmanali] 对检测奶酪缺陷的技能表示赞赏，认为这是独特的手工艺，体现了人工检测的非凡价值。
• [paulorlando] 对生产过程中变化的认知提出疑问，认为经过50年的经验积累，应该能够看到一致的结果，但事实似乎并非如此。
• [jacobgkau] 对不同质量的奶酪销售方式感兴趣，指出根据质量不同，奶酪会以不同品牌或无品牌形式出售，强调了质量分级的重要性。
• [dfxm12] 关注奶酪生产中的人为因素，质疑是否存在偏袒，并询问消费者是否会选择特定生产商的Parmigiano Reggiano。
• [saltcured] 提到一个可能的故事，关于人类专家通过嗅觉而非听觉判断奶酪质量，质疑检测技术的实际依据。
• [fracus] 认为手工检测似乎比看起来简单，只需要通过敲击判断是否中空，质疑手工技能的复杂性。
• [verelo] 通过个人故事分享了意大利文化中的“piano piano”（慢慢来）概念，表达了对传统价值观的喜爱。
• [taxicabjesus] 分享了因食用工业化奶酪导致健康问题的经历，强调了传统制作方法的重要性，特别是避免工业添加剂的使用。

补充讨论：
• 手工制作与技术应用之间的争议是主要焦点，部分评论者认为手工代表了传统和文化价值，而另一些人则认为技术能提高效率且不影响质量。
• 对奶酪质量的判断标准和销售方式也有较多讨论，尤其是如何通过品牌和质量分级来区分不同产品。
• 文化背景和个人经历影响了对奶酪制作工艺的看法，部分评论者从个人经验出发，强调了传统奶酪的独特性和健康益处。

data.title: Arroyo (YC W23) has been acquired by Cloudflare
data.author: necubi
data.article_summary: 2025年4月10日，Arroyo团队宣布已被Cloudflare收购，旨在将无服务器SQL流处理功能引入Cloudflare开发者平台，并与Queues、Workers和R2等服务集成。Arroyo引擎将继续保持开源，并支持自托管。此次收购由Arroyo首席执行官Micah Wylde宣布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cloudflare的客户支持和销售服务质量，Arroyo技术方案的独特性与竞争，以及开源项目被商业公司收购的影响。

不同观点：
• **Cloudflare客户支持和销售问题**：
  - [tiffanyh] 认为Cloudflare的产品质量很高，但客户支持和销售服务极差，即使是付费用户也难以获得回应。她指出，只有在最初几周能得到支持，之后很难获得回应。
  - [prennert] 也表达了类似的观点，指出他们试图开设企业账户但无法联系到销售人员，认为如果Arroyo成为Cloudflare企业服务的一部分，普通用户可能难以使用。

• **Arroyo的技术竞争与独特性**：
  - [dm03514] 对Arroyo表示赞赏，认为其高性能和先进的流处理原语（如窗口和连接）有可能成为Flink和Spark Streaming的长期替代方案。但他提到Arroyo配置过于依赖UI，且API配置与其工作流程不匹配。
  - [rebanevapustus] 质疑Arroyo相对于Materialize或Feldera的独特性，认为Arroyo可能只是这些产品的子集。

• **开源项目收购的影响**：
  - [esafak] 关注Cloudflare在维护开源项目方面的声誉，质疑其是否能良好地维护所收购的开源项目。
  - [mentalgear] 提出更广泛的问题，讨论盈利公司收购开源项目的意图和开源项目的可购买性。

补充讨论：
• **其他反应**：
  - [Hansenq] 和 [jeffchao] 等对Micah及其团队表示祝贺，并对Arroyo加入Cloudflare表示期待。
  - [ambrood] 特别提到Iceberg catalog在R2上的应用，认为这是一个重要的进展。
  - [moonikakiss] 询问将流数据导入Iceberg/R2 catalog是否会成为优先事项。

争议焦点：
• Cloudflare的客户支持和销售服务的不可达性是主要争议点，付费用户对此表示强烈不满。
• Arroyo的技术独特性和其在市场中的定位也存在一定争议，部分用户对其相对于其他类似技术的优势持怀疑态度。

Blog
Updates from the Arroyo team
Arroyo is joining Cloudflare
April 10, 2025
Arroyo has been acquired by Cloudflare to bring serverless SQL stream processing to the Cloudflare Developer Platfrorm, integrated with Queues, Workers, and R2. The Arroyo Engine will remain open-source and self-hostable.
Micah Wylde
CEO of Arroyo

data.title: 2025 AI Index Report
data.author: INGELRII
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对AI报告及其相关问题的多角度讨论

不同观点：
• [技术实现与工具使用] simonw提到将报告中的CSV文件转换为SQLite数据库，以便使用Datasette Lite进行探索，并分享了相关链接。这体现了技术用户对数据处理和分析的需求。
• [模型比较与批评] trott对AI模型的比较提出质疑，特别是针对AlphaFold3与Vina、Gnina的比较，指出评估存在缺陷，并解释了原因。trott对AI持乐观态度，但认为具体比较不恰当。
• [国际竞争与地缘政治] janalsncm认为，尽管美国在AI领域处于领先地位，但中国正在缩小差距。作者指出大多数研究人员并不关注国家间的竞争，而是关注技术本身。同时，作者表达了对AI领域国家竞争的担忧。
• [AI实用性与局限] mrdependable分享了使用AI助手解决代码问题的挫折经历，指出LLM在处理特定问题时表现不如预期，且有时会陷入某种输出模式。
• [用户体验与网站设计] vander_elst提出了一个关于网站设计的元问题，质疑为何网站要增加打开图片的难度，并分析了可能的动机。
• [报告结构与内容] andai指出报告的结构是分章节的概述，每个章节都有独立的PDF，整个报告长达456页。这为读者提供了对报告规模和深度的认识。
• [环境影响与伦理问题] Signez对报告未包含环境影响章节表示惊讶，指出在欧洲，环境影响和伦理问题是讨论AI的重要话题。作者声明自己并非反AI，只是列举常见讨论点。
• [基准测试与性能提升] mentalgear认为，AI在基准测试中的性能提升可能是因为模型在这些测试上进行了微调，而非真正的广泛性能提升。
• [经济影响与市场表现] janpmz认为AI将提高生活水平和工作效率，但对这种效果如何反映在股票市场上不确定。
• [教育与师资准备] dartharva对K-12教育中引入AI表示好奇，质疑教师是否具备教授AI的能力。
• [报告质量与出版变化] joe_the_user对比了斯坦福过去的AI报告，认为现在的报告更像是大型新闻稿，缺乏实质性内容，并批评了公司将研究成果通过新闻发布的形式发布。
• [就业机会] colesantiago乐观地认为AI将创造新的就业机会。

补充讨论：
• 技术用户对数据处理工具的需求与分享（simonw）
• 对AI模型比较的质疑与解释（trott）
• 国际竞争与地缘政治对AI发展的影响（janalsncm）
• AI在实际问题解决中的局限性与用户体验问题（mrdependable）
• 网站设计对用户体验的影响（vander_elst）
• 报告的结构与内容深度（andai）
• 环境影响与伦理问题在AI讨论中的重要性（Signez）
• AI基准测试性能提升的背后原因（mentalgear）
• AI对经济和市场的影响（janpmz）
• K-12教育中引入AI的挑战与准备（dartharva）
• AI报告质量的变化与公司出版方式的批评（joe_the_user）
• AI对就业市场的潜在影响（colesantiago）

争议焦点：
• AI模型比较的恰当性与评估方法的合理性（trott vs 一般观点）
• 国际竞争与地缘政治在AI发展中的角色（janalsncm vs 一般观点）
• AI在实际问题解决中的有效性与用户体验（mrdependable vs 一般乐观看法）
• AI报告质量的变化与实质性内容的缺失（joe_the_user vs 一般观点）

data.title: We Designed TigerBeetle's Docs from Scratch
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: TigerBeetle团队从零开始重建了其文档网站，以符合TigerStyle和第一性原理的思维方式，而不仅限于数据库本身。他们最初使用Docusaurus来快速搭建文档原型，但发现它违背了团队的“零依赖”原则，引入了过多依赖和复杂性，且生成的额外文件影响了GitHub上的纯净展示，搜索功能也不理想。团队希望文档与数据库本身一样精益求精，因此决定创建一个简洁、清晰、快速的阅读体验。新的文档网站依赖Zig编译器，使用Pandoc进行Markdown解析，以确保内容在各种形式下的一致性，并通过Zig的构建系统实现增量更新。最终，文档网站不仅提升了外部用户体验，也优化了内部代码实现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：TigerBeetle团队决定自行构建文档网站的工程决策是否合理，以及其背后的理由是否充分。

不同观点：
• **质疑工程决策合理性**：
  - mtlynch认为该决策虽然可能出于趣味性，但从工程角度来看并不理想。他指出很多组织最终自行构建数据库是因为对现有解决方案的不合理要求，而TigerBeetle的许多理由（如CSP防XSS）显得牵强。
  - 他认为很多理由可以通过现有静态网站生成器（SSG）如Hugo、Pelican或Eleventy实现，无需从零构建。
  - 特别指出CSP防XSS的例子不具说服力，因为在一个文档网站上进行XSS攻击的价值不大，且有其他方法可以缓解此类风险。

• **支持独特性和风格**：
  - mahitethefish赞赏TigerBeetle的风格和独特性，认为他们做事方式不同且做得很好。
  
• **技术实现的讨论**：
  - Ericson2314认为TigerBeetle实际上是手动实现了一个类似Nix的系统，但质疑其对“零依赖原则”的坚持。他指出，使用预构建的Pandoc二进制文件与Nix尽量避免预构建二进制文件的精神相悖。
  
• **对自建解决方案的肯定**：
  - bognition赞赏TigerBeetle自建文档网站，认为在当前有众多现成工具的时代，这种做法让人耳目一新。他们认识到文档是产品的核心，而非附属部分。
  
• **对工具选择的讨论**：
